steps.name: Sample structure QC and total-RNA/duplication/low-depth diagnostics
steps.context: Raw integer Salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples) from rRNA-depleted total RNA libraries without UMIs. metadata.csv carries condition (treated/control). QC flags: duplication rate >60% in most libraries (no UMIs, so duplicates must not be removed as PCR artifact — they track true expression level); sample_01 has library size ~4x below median.
steps.question: Do the 12 heart samples (6 treated vs 6 control) separate by condition on a blind VST/PCA, and how do sample_01's low library size and the cohort's high duplication rate manifest in the sample structure?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC per R-0033 with the low-depth (R-0008) and high-duplication-without-UMIs (R-0078) flags explicitly kept as judgment calls, not defaults.

acceptance_criteria: Blind VST computed and PCA on top 500 variable genes produced, colored by condition
Sample-distance heatmap produced
Per-sample table of library size, detected gene count, and (if inferable) duplication proxy, with sample_01 and any duplication outliers flagged and reported, not removed by default
A stated, evidence-based decision on whether sample_01 is retained or excluded, with the size-factor argument noted

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.context: Design is unpaired, single batch, 2 groups of 6. Counts are raw integer Salmon gene-level counts; no batch or other covariate to include. Pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (the smallest group size). Set the condition factor's reference level explicitly to control so a positive log2FC means higher in treated.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated and 6 control heart samples, using a minimal pre-filter, DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization, and a Wald test with condition (reference level = control) as the sole factor?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage is the grounded method for a fixed 6v6 unpaired design on raw counts (R-0001, R-0009); explicit reference level per R-0036.

acceptance_criteria: Genes filtered to >=10 counts in >=6 samples before the model
DESeq2 run with design ~condition, reference level explicitly set to control, contrast named (condition, treated, control)
Wald test results table with unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering on
MA plot and dispersion plot produced as fit diagnostics
p-value histogram inspected and its shape reported before trusting the adjusted p-values
Number of genes tested after filtering and number of significant genes (padj<0.05) reported
Genes flagged NA by Cook's-distance count outlier detection reported separately from independent-filtering NAs

steps.name: Over-representation enrichment of significant DE genes (Hallmark, Reactome)
steps.context: The knowledge-check tool rejected a ranked fgsea pass for this situation and permits only over-representation analysis for this dataset/question combination. Use clusterProfiler enricher() with the set of significant genes (padj<0.05) as the query and the full set of genes tested by DESeq2 (post-filter) as the background universe — never the whole genome. Reference gene sets: MSigDB human Hallmark GMT (50 sets) and Reactome human pathways GMT, both present in the reference store. Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs with org.Hs.eg.db before testing and report the unmapped share.
steps.question: Which MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome pathways are over-represented among the genes significantly differentially expressed (padj<0.05) between treated and control heart samples?

grounding.reason: knowledge_check rejected fgsea preranked GSEA for this situation (rule R-0048) and named over-representation analysis with an explicit universe as the permitted enrichment method; step revised accordingly and passed the second check.

acceptance_criteria: Universe explicitly set to the DESeq2-tested gene set, not the whole genome
Gene sets restricted to the reference store's MSigDB Hallmark human GMT and Reactome human GMT (filtered to Homo sapiens), each with its release/version stated
Gene set size window of 15-500 members applied to each collection after intersecting with the universe
BH-adjusted p-values reported per collection, collections not merged into one list
If fewer than ~50 genes are significant at padj<0.05, state this explicitly in the report as a caveat on the power of the over-representation test
Share of query/universe gene symbols that failed to map to Entrez IDs reported

steps.context: Consolidate the QC findings (sample_01 low depth, high duplication without UMIs), the DESeq2 design and thresholds, the DE gene table, and the enrichment results into one report with full reproducibility metadata.

plan.title: Heart total-RNA treated vs control DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human heart samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch) with raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples). Total RNA after rRNA depletion without UMIs and a duplication rate above 60% in most libraries mean duplicate reads must be kept (they track expression level, not PCR artifact, absent UMIs) and reported rather than removed. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median and must be inspected on PCA/sample-distance plots and reported, not silently dropped. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure: sample-structure QC first (with the low-depth and high-duplication caveats explicit), a minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization inside the DESeq2 model, a Wald test with an explicit reference level (control), apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, BH-adjusted significance at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and a diagnostic report (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram). Because the knowledge check rejected a ranked fgsea pass here (the situation requires the discrete gene_list / over-representation route), the enrichment step uses clusterProfiler over-representation analysis of the significant (padj<0.05) genes against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome, using the tested genes as the universe, with a fallback plan stated if fewer than ~50 genes are significant.

steps.method: vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size/duplication rate table
keep gene with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
DE + enrichment report with QC caveats
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome (full ranked gene list, no p-value threshold)
Over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler) of significant DE genes (padj<0.05) against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome, universe = tested genes
